comparisons.peer_topic: Net Interest Income Growth and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income for 2024 was $8.06 billion, representing a 27% increase from 2023, driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates, partially offset by a decrease in deposits with banks.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS disclose Net Interest Income/Revenue performance, but show opposite trends. MS reports a 10% decrease in Wealth Management Net Interest Revenue to $7,313 million, driven by lower average sweep deposits. In contrast, GS reports a 27% increase in consolidated Net Interest Income to $8.06 billion, driven by higher interest income from trading assets and investments. While MS's decline is linked to deposit dynamics (sweep deposits), GS's growth is linked to trading assets and higher average interest rates.

sentences.text: Net interest revenues of $7,313 million in 2024 decreased 10% compared with the prior year, primarily due to lower average sweep deposits, partially offset by higher yields on our investment portfolio and lending growth.

Net interest income in the consolidated statements of earnings was $8.06 billion for 2024, 27% higher than 2023, reflecting an increase in interest income, partially offset by an increase in interest expense.

The increase in interest income primarily related to trading assets and investments (each reflecting the impact of higher average balances and higher average interest rates), collateralized agreements and other interest-earning assets (each reflecting the impact of higher average interest rates), partially offset by a decrease in interest income related to deposits with banks (reflecting the impact of lower average balances).

comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income was $54.9 billion, flat year-over-year, due to lower margin compression and deposits in BWM, higher revolving balances in Card Services, and timing impacts from First Republic in Home Lending.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM report on Net Interest Income/Revenue trends where deposit dynamics played a key role, but outcomes differed. MS's Wealth Management net interest revenue decreased 10% primarily due to 'lower average sweep deposits.' JPM's overall net interest income was flat at $54.9 billion, with a decline in Banking & Wealth Management (BWM) driven by 'lower average deposits' and margin compression. MS specifically cites sweep deposits, while JPM cites lower average deposits in BWM as a headwind, though JPM also notes offsets from higher revolving balances in Card Services.
